title: God's Provision
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
What if everything you needed to live well was already available to you, and you just didn't know how to access it? And what if the reason so many people feel like they're falling short has nothing to do with what they lack?

In this sermon, Ps Keith Ainge unpacks a single verse from 2 Peter that carries more weight than most people realise. He works through six ideas packed into just 27 words, and the way he connects ancient scripture to everyday life, from flat-pack furniture to a Ford Prefect in the backyard, makes it genuinely hard to look away. There's something here about the difference between knowing about someone and actually knowing them, and why that distinction might be the most important thing you explore this year.

Sit down and give this one a watch.

title: The Guarantee
speaker: Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the Christian life you've been living is actually just the starting line, not the finish line? And what if there's a genuine guarantee attached to how you build from here?

In this sermon, Andrew Cartledge opens up a series through one of the most overlooked corners of the New Testament, and the question he keeps coming back to is both simple and uncomfortable: are you burying what you've been given, or actually doing something with it? He draws on some unexpected stories, a cringe-worthy high school athletics moment, a workplace analogy, and a parable that most people think they already know, to frame something that might reframe how you think about faith entirely. If you've ever felt like your spiritual life is running but going nowhere, this is worth your time.

Watch now and find out what the guarantee actually says.

title: Authority to Grow
speaker: Ron Spence
blurb:
What if the thing holding you back from growing isn't a lack of effort or faith, but something you've never thought to question? And what if the answer has been hiding in plain sight in a story about a Roman soldier?

In this episode, Pastor Ron Spence takes an unexpected path through Robin Williams, Elmer Fudd, and a centurion who understood something that most people never figure out. He unpacks why so many people stay stuck, why imagination can be more dangerous than circumstance, and what it actually looks like to carry the kind of authority that changes things. This one moves around a lot, but it keeps landing in the same place, and by the end you'll see exactly why that place matters.

Hit play and find out what a Roman soldier knew about spiritual authority that most Christians are still missing.

title: Harvest Church Sunday Service 10:30AM
blurb:
What if the biggest barrier to doing something meaningful isn't your lack of resources, your lack of confidence, or even your lack of calling, but simply the way you've been thinking about your role? And what if a story you've heard a hundred times actually contains something you've completely missed?

In this episode, Pastor Joel brings a fresh set of eyes to one of the most familiar miracles in the Bible, and the result is genuinely uncomfortable in the best way. He traces a shift in how Jesus related to the people around him, a shift that reframes what it means to belong to a church community. Along the way he shares stories from his own life that are honest, funny, and surprisingly convicting. By the end, you'll find yourself asking a question you might not have considered before.

Hit play and find out what Jesus actually said when the people around him pointed out a problem they expected someone else to fix.

title: 1. The Revelation of Jesus
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Revelation is not a code to crack but a Christ to behold. It was written to comfort, not confuse; 

to unveil Christ, not conceal truth

In this message, we tackle the most misunderstood book in the Bible. Discover why Revelation isn't about fear or end-times speculation, but about unveiling Jesus Christ Himself.

Learn 7 essential principles for properly reading Revelation, understand the first-century context that changes everything, and witness John's magnificent vision of the glorified Christ. This foundational message reveals why Revelation has been a source of hope for believers for 2,000 years.

Perfect for anyone wanting to understand Revelation through Scripture rather than popular fiction. Come see Jesus as "the Alpha and the Omega" - faithful in the past, sovereign in the present, and triumphant in the future.

title: I Live Generously
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Title: The Secret to True Happiness | Living Generously

Description:

We all want to be happy—but why does happiness seem so elusive, even when we get what we've been chasing? In this powerful message, we explore one of Jesus' most radical teachings: "It is more blessed to give than to receive" (Acts 20:35). True happiness isn't found in having more—it's found in giving more. Drawing from Scripture, this sermon challenges the Western mindset of more money = more happiness and reveals that Jesus' formula of more generosity = more happiness holds the key to a fulfilled life. Discover how generosity with your time, talent, and treasure can transform your life and the lives of those around you.

title: Reaching the World
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this powerful message, we explore the transformative journey of loving God, growing together, and reaching the world. The central theme is love—loving God with all our heart, soul, and mind, and extending that love to our neighbors and the world. Join us as we delve into the profound concept of agape love, not just as a theological term, but as a practical guide for our lives. Discover how discipleship and evangelism are key to living out this calling, and how we can impact the world by living selflessly, putting others before ourselves. Whether you're new to faith or have been walking with Christ for years, this message will inspire you to deepen your understanding and practice of love in your everyday life.

title: Growing Together
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Faith isn't meant to be a solo journey—we grow stronger together. Matthew 22 calls us to love God and love others, and Acts 2:42 shows us a church devoted to teaching, fellowship, and prayer. Real growth happens in genuine relationships, where we sharpen one another like iron. Are we willing to invest, be vulnerable, and serve sacrificially? Let's build a community that reflects Christ's love!

title: Loving God
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this inspiring sermon, Pastor Andrew launches a new series at Harvest Church, emphasising the core mission of the church: "Loving God, Growing Together, Reaching the World." He breaks down the importance of embracing these principles as a unified community, stressing that a mission only has power when fully understood and lived out by everyone. Through a deep dive into loving God with all our heart, soul, and mind, Pastor Andrew challenges the congregation to commit to a transformational Christian lifestyle. Join us as we explore how these simple yet profound concepts can lead to personal growth and a stronger communal bond.

title: Come to the Table
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge, Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: Join us for a powerful sermon exploring the profound significance of the table in Scripture as a place of reconciliation and unity. Discover how the early church, amidst a backdrop of division and tension, demonstrated radical equality at the table through the unifying power of the Gospel. This message delves into stories of biblical reconciliation, such as Joseph and his brothers, David and Mephibosheth, and Jesus' interactions during the Last Supper. Be inspired by the table's symbolism as a place of grace, restoration, and forgiveness, culminating in the ultimate table of reconciliation—the cross. We invite you to partake in communion and embrace the healing and unity offered through Christ. Don't miss this transformative journey of acceptance, forgiveness, and renewal.

title: Socially Acceptable
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: "Are we desensitised to 'socially acceptable sins'? Proverbs 6:16-19 reminds us that what society normalises may still grieve God's heart. From gossip to greed, this message challenges us to examine our lives, repent, and align with God's standards. Let's pursue revival through holiness and prayer, keeping our eyes on Christ—the ultimate antidote to sin."

title: Month of Prayer - Revival
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Are we truly hungry for God? Psalm 63:1 reminds us of David's deep thirst for God's presence. Revival begins with conviction, repentance, and prayer. Acts 2 shows the power of unity and hunger for God. What are we willing to sacrifice for revival? Let's make prayer central and seek Him wholeheartedly.

title: The Heart of an Armour Bearer
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Are you ready to embrace the heart of an armor bearer? Inspired by 1 Samuel 14, this message challenges us to step out in faith, trust God, and move in unity. Just as Jonathan's armor bearer said, 'I am with you, heart and soul,' we're called to support one another and see God do extraordinary things through us.

title: Armour Bearers
speaker: Ps David McCracken
blurb: Ps David spoke prophetically over the life, direction and future of our church as well as brought insight to many individuals. The overall theme, armour bearers release the victory. This is an important word for Harvest Church

title: How to Talk about Jesus
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: We're reminded of our calling to share the good news of Jesus with others. This message emphasizes the importance of personal evangelism, rooted in Isaiah 6:8 - 'Here I am. Send me.' We're all called to be evangelists in our daily lives, not just those with a specific gift. The main barriers to sharing our faith often stem from fear - fear of inadequacy, losing reputation, rejection, or appearing hypocritical. To overcome these, we're encouraged to follow Jesus' example of compassion and love for others. The message outlines five key components for effective evangelism: prayer, loving others, sharing the gospel message, telling our personal story, and being obedient despite the results. We're reminded that our job is to sow seeds, while God brings the harvest.

title: Life Lessons from Golf
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this engaging exploration, we're challenged to examine our integrity through the lens of golf and biblical stories. Joseph's unwavering integrity in the face of temptation from Potiphar's wife serves as a powerful example. We're reminded that integrity often comes at a cost, but ultimately leads to greater rewards. The message emphasizes that our true character is revealed when no one is watching, drawing parallels between the hidden moments on a golf course and our daily lives. We're encouraged to 'take the penalty' and do what's right, even when it's difficult, trusting that God sees our hearts and will honor our faithfulness.

title: Great Faith
speaker: Ps Matt Heins
blurb: In this powerful message, we're reminded of the importance of cultivating great faith in our lives. The story of Joseph from Genesis 43 serves as a backdrop to illustrate how we can sometimes get caught up in 'donkey mentalities' - focusing on small, insignificant issues while missing God's bigger picture. We're encouraged to shift our perspective, understanding that God is always moving in our lives, even when we can't see it. The message emphasizes the need to activate our faith through prayer and immersion in God's Word, reminding us that God delights not only in our worship but also in our requests. This teaching challenges us to maintain a healthy disconnect from constant discouragement, drawing inspiration from biblical figures who persevered through trials. As we reflect on these insights, we're inspired to nurture a faith that's ready for the big things God has in store for us.

title: The Lord is Near
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this powerful exploration of Philippians 4, we're reminded of the transformative power of joy and contentment in our Christian walk. The central message revolves around the profound truth that 'the Lord is near.' This simple yet profound statement serves as the foundation for overcoming anxiety, finding peace, and living a life of rejoicing. We're encouraged to shift our focus from worldly concerns to the presence of God, bringing all our worries to Him in prayer with thanksgiving. This practice unlocks a peace that surpasses all understanding, guarding our hearts and minds in Christ Jesus. The message challenges us to examine how we interpret and apply Scripture, urging us to consider the full context rather than isolated verses. It's a call to root our contentment and joy not in circumstances, but in our relationship with Christ.

title: Tackling The Tensions
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb: In this powerful message, we explore the concept of divine tensions in our faith journey. We're reminded that not all tension is negative - in fact, it's often necessary for growth and strength. Just as a suspension bridge needs tension to function, our spiritual lives often require us to hold seemingly contradictory truths in balance. The Bible itself is full of these 'divine tensions' or paradoxes - like being both a new creation and still being transformed, or experiencing both suffering and glory. Rather than seeing these as contradictions, we're encouraged to approach them with curiosity and humility, like Moses approaching the burning bush. By using our 'spiritual eyes' and stepping closer to investigate, we may find that these tensions are actually holy ground where God reveals Himself to us.
